description: Details pursuant to the discharge of Conditions 2 (Materials) and 6 (Tree Protection) of planning permission ref. 43419/APP/2014/3879, dated 21-01-2015 (Erection of two detached houses with dormers and integral garages, new crossovers and associated external works (involving demolition of the existing house))
decision_conditions: The details submitted in relation to Condition 2 fail to provide adequate information on the external materials and finishes of the approved dwellings. The submission only includes limited details of hard landscaping surfaces and does not cover the principal building materials required by the condition. The application is therefore contrary to Policy D3 of the London Plan (2021) and Policy DMHB 11 of the Hillingdon Local Plan Part Two (2020).

The application confirms that the applicant has breached planning conditions 6 (Tree Protection Plan) of planning permission ref. 43419/APP/2014/3879 by removing trees from the site without the prior written consent of the Local Planning Authority, contrary to the planning permission and Paragraph 136 of the National Planning Policy Framework (2024), Policy G7 of The London Plan (2021), and Policy DMHB 14 of Hillingdon Council's Local Plan Part Two Development Management Policies (2020).

It is noted that the building works in relation to the original approval have been completed without discharging all the conditions. As trees have been removed without consent, it may not be possible to discharge condition 6 and a variation of the original condition or full planning permission may be required. In order to proceed with this route, further information within the s73 would need to include details of the trees that were remove and their value. It is advisable to seek advise from an Arboriculturist prior to resubmitting.

Furthermore, it is noted that no details have been provided on the materials used in the finish of the dwelling house. This could also be addressed through a s73 application. Any follow up application on this matter would need to include specific details on the facing materials used in the finished dwelling.
